chunks: Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) narrated from Qum in Rajab of the year 339 A.H. that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed him, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of al-Sakuni, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon him).
He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Poverty is close to being disbelief, and jealousy/envy is close to overpowering destiny.'
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between poverty and disbelief in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq places this hadith in the context of spiritual pathology, where extreme material deprivation can lead to a loss of faith, and envy acts as a catalyst that disrupts the natural flow of divine decree. This reflects the Shia understanding of the interplay between human agency and predestination, emphasizing that while destiny is fixed, certain traits like envy can alter its manifestation. The narration underscores the practical necessity of maintaining spiritual resilience against both economic hardship and internal psychological corruption.
